changes: lattice check now reports explicit managed asset root diagnostics in JSON and text output, including metadataRoot, assetRoot, gitRoot, pathsRelativeTo, and split-root status.
usage: Run lattice check or lattice check --json; read assetRoot as the base for managed asset relPath, applied paths, and manifestPath before running check --apply.
expectedOutcome: Users can tell whether managed asset paths are rooted at the metadata/asset root or only related to gitRoot diagnostics before applying drift fixes.
actualTranscript: node packages/main/dist/cli.js check --json exposed metadataRoot/assetRoot/gitRoot/pathsRelativeTo/assetRootGitRootSplit; node packages/main/dist/cli.js check printed Paths guidance before Drift and marked gitRoot as same as assetRoot in this worktree.
outcomeDiff: Expected path-base diagnostics matched actual output; existing DRIFT status remains visible because the story intentionally clarifies roots without applying managed asset changes.
limitations: none — fully covered by build, npm test, focused wrapper-root smoke, JSON/text transcript, and four reviewer lanes
pitfalls: Do not interpret gitRoot as the managed asset write root; asset writes remain assetRoot-relative even when gitRoot is shown for diagnostic clarity.
